name: TidyTuesday
description: A weekly community data project: every Monday a curated, cleaned dataset lands in a public repository with a readme describing its columns and provenance, and thousands of people publish visualisations of it. Running since 2018, so the repository is now a well-documented archive of ~400 tidy datasets on almost every subject.

license.name: per-dataset; each week's readme names the original source and its terms
license.redistribution: the repo is a teaching mirror - cite the original source

probes.description: An arbitrary historical week's data file

recipes.title: List every week and its files
recipes.code:
for y in 2024 2025 2026; do
  curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/contents/data/$y" \
    | python3 -c "import json,sys;[print(d['path']) for d in json.load(sys.stdin)]"
done

gotchas.trap: Weekly folders hold the data files and a readme.md, but the readme is the only description of the columns.
gotchas.fix: Fetch data/<year>/<date>/readme.md alongside the data; it names the original source, which is what you should cite.

gotchas.trap: The datasets are cleaned for teaching, sometimes subset or simplified relative to the original.
gotchas.fix: Use it to learn the shape of a dataset, then go to the source for analysis you will publish.
